next_round_constraints: Keep fractional = 0 (no fractional dynamics) for this series in the next round.

Prioritize observation maps that preserve short lag: delayed_I with delay_weeks constrained to {1,2}; avoid delay_weeks >= 3 unless paired with a compensating mechanism explicitly intended to shift phase.

Favor simpler compartment structures unless a change is specifically aimed at correcting a clearly identified phase/amplitude bias; treat SEIRS and SEIR as primary candidates, with SEIHR only if observation is strictly H and complexity is otherwise controlled.
If exploring alternatives, vary only one axis at a time (structure OR observation_map OR delay) to isolate what improves rolling consistency.
observed_failure_modes: Delay sensitivity: delayed_I with 3-week delay degrades vs 2-week, suggesting the effective reporting/clinical lag is shorter and over-delaying misaligns peaks/turning points.

Structure mismatch across splits: SEIR/SEIHR variants show different relative behavior between single validation vs rolling splits, indicating some templates may fit the held-out window but generalize less consistently across rolling origins.

Over-parameterization risk: adding hospitalization compartment and/or mixing I+H does not appear to yield robust gains relative to simpler delayed_I mapping, implying extra degrees of freedom may be fitting noise rather than stable dynamics.
Potential observation-map mismatch: direct H or I+H mappings may distort amplitude/phase for this age group’s hospitalization-rate series compared with an incidence-proxy (I) plus short delay.
feedback.proposer_instruction: For the next round on 5–17 yr, center proposals around SEIRS/SEIR with observation_map=delayed_I and delay_weeks in {1,2} (include both to test whether 1-week lag better aligns turning points). De-emphasize SEIHR and mixed I+H mappings unless you can justify them as correcting a specific systematic bias (e.g., persistent phase shift) and keep the rest of the spec minimal. Make proposals that change only one component relative to the current best (SEIRS + delayed_I + 2-week delay) to improve rolling-origin consistency rather than optimizing a single validation window.
